classification.difficultyReason: Choose alternate-segment sectors and link them to familiar parallel-line, isosceles and equal-tangent angle facts; the hardest parts require two or three linked deductions.

content.prompt: Find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$, giving reasons. In the diagrams, tangents are drawn at $S$, $T$ and $U$.

spec.description: Inscribed FGT with FG parallel to the tangent at T.
spec.mathematics: Unit-circle F260°,G100°,T0°; FG and tangent are vertical; given GTM50°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, named points and unknowns; no calculated answers.

answer.worked:
$\alpha=50^\circ$ (alternate segment theorem).

Since $FG\parallel LM$, $\beta=\alpha=50^\circ$ (alternate angles).

The adjacent angles on the straight tangent line give
$$\gamma=180^\circ-50^\circ-50^\circ=80^\circ.$$

answer.worked:
$TA=TB$, so $\beta=70^\circ$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).

$\alpha=\beta=70^\circ$ (alternate segment theorem).

$$\gamma=180^\circ-70^\circ-70^\circ=40^\circ$$ (angle sum of triangle $TAB$).

spec.description: Tangents PT/PS and equal chords TS/SF; obtuse TSF110°.
spec.mathematics: T160°,S90°,F20° give equal chords and inscribed TSF110°; P is the exact intersection of tangents.

answer.worked:
$TS=SF$, so $\angle STF=\angle TFS=\beta$.

$$2\beta+110^\circ=180^\circ,\qquad\beta=35^\circ.$$

$\alpha=\angle PTS=\angle TFS=35^\circ$ (alternate segment theorem).

answer.worked:
$\alpha=130^\circ$ (alternate segment theorem for chord $ST$).

Since $B,T,H$ are collinear,
$$\angle BTS=180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ.$$

$BS=BT$ (tangents from $B$), so $\angle BST=50^\circ$. Hence
$$\beta=180^\circ-50^\circ-50^\circ=80^\circ.$$

spec.description: Triangle ABC circumscribes the circle at U,T,S; inscribed triangle SUT.

answer.worked:
$\alpha=\angle UST=50^\circ$ (alternate segment theorem).

$AU=AT$ (tangents from $A$), so both base angles of $\triangle AUT$ are $50^\circ$. Therefore
$$\beta=180^\circ-2(50^\circ)=80^\circ.$$

$BU=BS$ (tangents from $B$), so
$$\gamma=\frac{180^\circ-70^\circ}{2}=55^\circ.$$
